title: Broadcasting Services Amendment (Healthy Kids Advertising) Bill 2024
short_title: Broadcasting Services Amendment (Healthy Kids Advertising) Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would stop unhealthy food marketing on certain TV and radio services and on online platforms, including narrowcasting and subscription services.

It would create a general ban on such marketing online, applying to both content providers and those who pay for the content, with a definition of unhealthy food based on a 2018 COAG Health Council guide and allowing the minister to add more foods.
Courts could impose penalties of up to $550,000 or 5% of a large corporation's turnover from unhealthy food products, and the operation would be reviewed after four years.
changes: Prohibits airing unhealthy food marketing on TV and radio between 6am and 9:30pm local time.
Bans unhealthy food marketing online at all hours.
Defines unhealthy food using the 2018 COAG Health Council guide and lets the minister add more foods.
Sets penalties of up to $550,000 or 5% of turnover for large corporations.
Requires a review after four years.
summary.affected: Children and the general public, along with broadcasters, online content providers, and advertisers who pay for such marketing.
